subject: AcmeHealth Private/VPC discovery - post-call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Sanchez <elena.sanchez@acmehealth.com>, Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: AcmeHealth Private/VPC discovery - post-call recap and next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the candid conversation. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Pain points you shared:
- PHI data residency: all patient data must remain inside AcmeHealth VPCs and cannot be persisted to a third-party shared service.
- Network restrictions: only outbound TLS to a limited set of IPs is allowed; egress through a proxy is mandatory in some environments.
- Air-gap needs for specific deployments (lab environments) where internet connectivity is not permitted.
- Latency sensitivity for real-time charting workflows (95th percentile latency target < 250ms).

Goals you described:
- Run inference on-prem or within a private VPC under AcmeHealth control.
- Integrate with existing KMS and centralized audit logs.
- Meet SOC 2 / HITRUST posture and provide evidence for security review.

What Redwood can do (high level):
- Private deployment (VPC peering or private control plane) with customer-managed networking and KMS integrations.
- Air-gapped on-prem option; our SEs can provide an install bundle and offline artifacts for your security team to validate.
- Smart routing/fallback rules to keep services online while honoring residency constraints.
- Observability hooks and token-level cost/latency dashboards for your SREs and security reviewers.

Action items / next steps:
1) Camila to share the minimal network port/IP list and the private deploy checklist (we said we'd attach the checklist).
2) Elena/Rajiv to share the internal network diagram and procurement timeline.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra and security teams next week (Camila + Marissa + Acme infra/security).
4) Procurement to confirm contract review owner and expected procurement window.

Attachments: network-diagram.pdf (placeholder), redwood-private-deploy-checklist.xlsx

If I've missed anything, please call it out — otherwise I'll book the deep-dive for next Wednesday (propose 10:00am PT) pending your calendars.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0147

Thanks Marissa — this is great and accurate. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The air-gapped requirement applies to our R&D lab environment only; production workloads must remain in our AWS accounts (us-east-1) with VPC endpoints.
- For the production VPCs we can allow outbound to a short allowlist (we'll need IPs and FQDNs). Proxy sits at 10.12.0.1 for outbound.egress.
- Latency target is 95th < 250ms for the charting pipeline, but we can tolerate slightly higher for batch reports.

Procurement note: procurement@acmehealth.com will lead contracting. They asked if you have a standard MSA + SOW template and if DocuSign is supported.

We can do the technical deep-dive next Wednesday 10:00am PT — Rajiv and our cloud infra lead (TBD) will join.

-Elena
Director of Data Platforms | AcmeHealth

Elena — thanks for the clarifications. Added a few technical notes below and included the checklist as promised.

Technical notes / ask list (minimal):
- Required outbound: TLS to the following IPs/FQDNs (we'll provide consolidated allowlist): 34.120.45.9, 34.120.45.10, pkg.redwood-inference.com (for package manifests).
- Ports: 443 outbound for control-plane telemetry; 22 only for scheduled maintenance windows (by exception).
- If you route outbound via proxy at 10.12.0.1, please confirm authentication mechanism (NTLM / proxy auth) and whether metadata service egress is allowed for instance role credentialing.
- KMS: we support AWS KMS and customer-provided HSMs. We'll surface required IAM roles and minimal policy snippets in the deep-dive.
- Air-gap: for the lab environment we can provide an offline bundle + validation checklist. No outbound calls are required for inference once the artifact is installed; diagnostics can be run manually.

Attached: redwood-private-deploy-checklist.xlsx (contains port lists, firewall rules, install order, and offline bundle steps).
